newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms eye additional 56,000 T U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms eye additional 56,000 T U.S. wheat.

text.p: Philippine flour mills plan to buy an additional 56,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for their November and December requirements, traders said on Wednesday.

Earlier in the day, traders had said they had received tender invitations for 41,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 14 percent protein content and another 12,000 tonnes of western white wheat from a group of Philippine flour mills.
Two traders from major commodity firms said they expected Philippine flour millers to buy at least 200,000 tonnes of wheat for their November and December requirements.
"I think U.S. wheat prices have reached bottom. Now is the time to buy," a senior trader in a Japanese commodity house told Reuters.
"Philippine millers have to order now to meet their requirements in the next two months," said another senior trader in a European commodity firm.
Wheat prices in Chicago closed 1-3/4 to 7-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 7-3/4 at $4.21-3/4 on local and fund selling.

The U.S. Agriculture deparment said on Tuesday it expected world wheat output in 1996/1997 at 581 million tonnes, up from 579.5 million forecast in September and nearly 45 million tonnes higher than 1995/1996.
